title: Show HN: A Claude Code plugin that plays a song and shows a startup card

item.title: Show HN: A Claude Code plugin that plays a song and shows a startup card

sources.text:
startup-song 🎵
A Claude Code plugin that plays a few seconds of a random song every time you start Claude Code.
Rotates through genres, one per session:
pop → hip hop → retro hits → pop …
For each one, it searches the
iTunes Search API
(free, no key) and plays a random song from the
top 10
results.
Shows a startup card above the prompt while it plays:
Coding streak
: days in a row you've started Claude Code
Repo status
: branch, changed files, ahead/behind, last commit
On this day
: one event from
Wikipedia's on-this-day feed
(grim ones skipped)
The card goes away when the song ends. Press
Esc
at an empty prompt to stop it early.
/today
opens the card again.
Uses
zero tokens
: no model call, just two web requests, two local
git
commands and an audio clip.
Audio is Apple's official 30-second preview of each track; nothing is downloaded or stored.
Install
/plugin install startup-song --marketplace heyyviv/claude-boot-beats
Or try it from a local copy:
claude --plugin-dir ./claude-startup-song
Settings
Change these in
/config
:
Setting
Default
What it does
genres
pop, hip hop, retro hits
Comma-separated search words, used in turn
seconds
10
How long to play (max 30)
Requirements
macOS (playback uses
afplay
). On Linux/Windows the plugin stays silent.
Internet at startup. Offline, it simply plays nothing.
